subtopic: Parents pressure on career or marriage
passage:
Omkar's father, Tushar, slid a folder across the table. "Look at this biodata. Good family, works in a bank."

"Papa, I'm twenty-four. I told you I want two more years."

"Two years! Your cousin was married at twenty-four."

"I know. I'm not against marriage. I want to finish my articleship and know my own mind first. And I'd want someone comfortable with me working late."

"People talk, beta. Your mother is anxious."

"What is she anxious about, exactly?"

Tushar lowered the paper. "That you'll be alone when we're gone."

Omkar was quiet. "I didn't know that. It's a real worry. Can we agree that I'll tell you the moment I meet someone, and you won't send my biodata anywhere until then?"

"...Let me talk to your mother."

qa.q: What job does the person on the biodata have?
What worry lies behind Tushar's push for marriage?
qa.a: Tushar fears that Omkar will be alone when the parents are gone, and Omkar's mother is anxious about it too.

qa.q: How does Omkar's way of answering help?
qa.a: Omkar stays calm, gives a timeline and what matters, listens to the fear behind the push, and proposes a clear agreement instead of lying or giving in.

qa.q: How might Omkar's mother feel about this conversation?
qa.a: Probably anxious about talk and the future, wanting reassurance more than a fight. Hearing that Omkar takes the worry seriously may soften it.

grounding: Family pushes biodata while Omkar wants time; Omkar speaks calmly about timeline and values and listens to the father's fears.

subtopic: Parents pressure on career or marriage
passage:
Counsellor's note, women's college, 3 February
Afreen, final-year B.Com, came in upset. Her family has been sharing biodatas every weekend and arranged two "just tea" visits this month. She said she had been agreeing to each meeting "to end the conversation", then feeling trapped. She wants two years of work first.
We practised what she might say. She wrote it in her own words: "I'm not refusing marriage. I want to work for two years first, and I want someone who respects that. What are you most worried about?" She practised the last question three times; it mattered to her to listen too.
Today she came back. She had spoken to her parents on Sunday. Her father worried about her "getting too old"; her mother worried about what relatives say. They agreed to pause visits until after her exams and talk again then. She looked tired, and much lighter.
Disha, counsellor

qa.q: How many "just tea" visits were arranged this month?
How had Afreen been feeling after agreeing to each meeting?
qa.a: Trapped and upset, because she agreed only to end the conversation.

qa.q: What made Afreen's prepared words a wise approach?
qa.a: They stated her timeline and values calmly and ended with a real question about her parents' worries, so she listened as well as spoke.

qa.q: What worries did Afreen's parents share?
qa.a: Her father worried about her "getting too old" and her mother about what relatives say.

grounding: Shows family pressure to marry and speaking calmly about one's timeline and values while listening to the parents' fears, instead of agreeing to escape.

subtopic: Parents pressure on career or marriage
passage:
Sunday, late
Amma put another biodata next to my plate at lunch. Engineer, Chennai, "good family". The fifth since Pongal.
I almost said, "I'm already seeing someone," just to make it stop. It would've worked for a month. Then what, invent a whole person?
Instead I put down my spoon and said, "Amma, Appa, I'm not saying never. I'm twenty-two. I want to finish my CA first. And when I marry, I want someone who's fine with me working late." Amma's face tightened. "People are asking."
Jeevan anna, of all people, said, "Let her finish, Amma. She's not running away."
Appa asked what I'd look for in a person. Nobody has ever asked me that. I told him: kind, curious, not scared of my ambition. He nodded slowly.
Nothing's settled. But nobody slammed a door.
— Manjula

qa.q: How many biodatas had come since Pongal?
Why did Manjula almost say "I'm already seeing someone"?
qa.a: She felt cornered and tired of the pressure, and the lie looked like a quick way to make it stop.

qa.q: What did Manjula say instead of lying?
qa.a: She calmly explained her timeline, finishing CA first, and what she wants in a partner, and answered Appa's question honestly.
What people say: relatives are asking, which is why her face tightens.

grounding: Illustrates pressure to marry and choosing calm honesty about one's timeline and values over a lie to escape the conversation.
